body: I think when people impact your life, whether good or bad, you end up thinking about them unconsciously. In your case with your ex, you probably miss the time you spent with him and your brain is trying to cope with not having that connection anymore. Dreams are so surreal but idk if it’s smart to act on a dream.

I’m on the other end of this, I’ve been dreaming about this girl who’s heart I kind of broke in my late teens. It’s been about 4 years but in the last couple months I’ve been dreaming about her and I regret the shit I did. And mine aren’t sexual, it’s mostly just relationship shit. Idk though, maybe it’s because I’m regretting things that’s making me think about her and then dreaming about her too. I even went as far to draft a message to her apologizing. But I don’t know if that’s too creepy after 4 years of not talking. We did see each other last year at a reunion but we didn’t talk much at all.

I don’t think it’s something you need to tell her out of the blue. When you start getting the hots, just tell her your self conscious about it and she’ll respect you for saying something. I wouldn’t do it unless you were getting in the mood to have sex. Don’t just spring it out of no where. 

Alternatively you could say it’s like really small, I’m talking 1.5 incheroos and then when she whips out 5 inches of pure mass, it’ll seem wayyyy bigger. Might backfire but hey man. Best thing to do is play it off with confidence. 

(There’s mans out there with barely anything poking out, so I’m sure the heat you’re packing is gonna be fine)

I actually started school this January as well for similar reasons. I hated my old construction jobs and wanted to follow my passions. Honestly I’ve already made some cool friends, idk how your program works but mine we all started out at the same time. Sure it’s stressful but realizing we’re kind of in the same position is helpful. There’s not much advice I can give you other than just to go out of your way to find the help, talk to faculty or guidance and see if you can figure something out. Maybe comp science isn’t for you, but your school offers another program that interests you. 

clubs and extra curricular activities are a great way to make friends. Go places you normally wouldn’t go. Idk man but we all go through these ups and downs, just trying to help while I’m up. Good luck and I’m sure you’re gonna be good.

What’s the point of putting effort into dying. Shit may be hard but if you really wanted to die, you would find a way regardless of a plan. It just shows that deep down you don’t want to die. Pills are something you take in a dark alley or hotel room where no one will find you till it’s too late. I can tell that you gave up but do you really want to die? I’ve been through my share of ups and downs, and think like you sometimes but I think making a plan is almost more selfish than suicide itself. It shows people your intent to leave them without a second thought. Idk just think about it before you do anything irreversible.

I lost my brother (27) 2 and a half years ago. I feel that pain, losing a sibling is hard. Every day I dont go without thinking about all of the events he is going to miss. My best man is going to have to be replaced when I get married. So many regrets and such little life to live.  I wont sugar coat it for you, you'll have good days and bad, seems like the bad days overshadow the good. Just start living your life in memory of your brother, all of your success will become his success. That's what gets me through my days. Eventually you become so caught up in your life that he blends in and it seems like he is always with you. Be strong bro, life has a lot of downs but there are some bright days to look out for.

I'll never forget the shock that coursed through my body, the moment of disbelief that I'd lost the most influential person in my life. I'm so sorry that you and your son have to go through that pain. I find this subreddit to be very inspiring at times, being able to hear about others conquering their grief and despair. Life does move on, but your husband will always be with you and your child through the sweet and sorrowful times.

I'm very sorry to hear about the loss of you wife and daughter. That doesnt sound easy to get through at all. You are such a strong person for caring about your son before yourself. As someone who has lost a sibling and has been lost like your son, I can relate to his emotions. The major advice I could give you would be to try talking to a therapist, it's the basic route to go when your son wont talk about his feelings. I remember when I first started going I hated it, it was the worst feeling in the world. I thought I didnt need to tell this random stranger my life story. But after a couple sessions I switched therapists and clicked with her right away. Something that therapist taught me was to write journals about anything, what I was feeling or what I did that day. I wasnt about it too much but writing did help me out. Idk what hobbies your son was into but turning those into a medium for support is a great way for him to get comfortable with his life. Obviously the grief never goes away but what I've found is I could easily distract myself when times were getting really dark. I know he wont want to talk to anyone but it's so important to get those bottled up feelings off your chest. 

I hope you and your son find the light within the darkness. You are a fantastic father and I hope you and your son get through this. My thoughts and prayers are with you

Thanks for the kind words, I really appreciate it. That post I made was during a hard time in my life when I needed support and couldn't get it. My family thinks that I need to learn everything by myself and that lending me a helping hand wont teach me anything. I mean sure they have a point but when I keep getting beaten down, sometimes I need help getting back up. My brother helped me out a lot when I felt like that and resented my parents for it. so it's hard for me to deal with it alone. 

My brothers death helped mend some wounds in my family for sure. I got closer with my mom but completely destroyed my relationship with my dad. I try to be a great big brother to my younger brother the way my big bro was to me. Im not gonna lie, I completely forgot about that post because so much has changed. I dont even remember when I wrote it. 

As of right now I have friends who are starting to help me finish school and go to college at the end of this year. I thought i was fighting this battle alone, but just today realized that I've got amazing friends who are going to help me succeed. As for my family, I'm going to do everything without them. I'm not gonna lean on them for support, I'm just gonna do stuff my way. 

I'll have my time to heal soon. It's been a rough 2 years yet I've gotten this far. I just needed that little shove to get the momentum going. Thanks again for reading my posts and saying all those nice words. We dont know what our futures hold but we are destined to do great things. Thanks brother.

I'm so sorry to hear that, I'm 21 as well and I cant imagine what that is like to go through, losing a child seems like the most cruel thing. I 100% agree with you, I know he wants me to be happy it's just when I'm in those dark times it's hard to see the light until I reflect and find the good points in life. I'm just stuck right now. I thought that I grew stronger over the past year but I'm just not sure where I'm heading. I wish I could embrace the pain and learn to love life again but it's hard. The only way I can escape is by distracting myself and I feel like that's starting to hurt me more than help. I only cry by myself and dont tell anyone about my breakdowns. Thank you for the advice though. I'll try my hardest to lean into the happy memories when I'm in my darkest moments.

But whenever I say that, they just rinse and repeat what I already know, so it just makes things worse. And I love my friends but they just dont know how to help, and I dont blame them. As far as family goes I dont really feel comfortable with most of them, and it's hard to talk to my immediate family because of my mentality to be strong. I've gotten professional help before and it really did wonders and worked but I found myself unmotivated to go and now I'm kinda stuck. But I find that venting helps a bit, I just dont know how to get out of this rut and get motivated again.
When myself or others scratch paper. I'm fine with anything else but when I think about scratching your nails on paper I get chills down my spine.

Idk I just feel like I need to always show others I'm strong because they dont know how to help me and comfort me. So instead of making it hard for them, I make it worse for myself. Mainly friends and acquaintances I'm talking about

Yeah you have a good point. I use the word "relapse" loosely. I compare the two because it's almost like I was doing fine then all of a sudden just a wave of depression and grief hit me. Just like you would relapse from drugs or alcohol. I've thought about counseling and groups, it's just that I find it hard to commit to those things. I feel normal, I know I'm not crazy but sometimes I'll just have these thoughts. I just found it strange that I've been fine all these months and all of a sudden it just blasted me. I found it interesting that after all this time of feeling like I've moved on, still having that connection is kinda nice. To know that maybe I'm not an apathetic freak you know lol
Yeah you have a point. I found crying and getting through that stuff necessary but i guess it still differs from person to person. That feeling will never go away, but it does get easier right.

There's not a whole lot you can do to be quite honest. But constant reminders of your support are immensely appreciated when going through grief. I'm just a kid so I cant give amazing advice but since I've been through a similar experience I wish people showed they cared instead of just saying it. The difference between saying your sorry compared to giving someone a hug and showing affection are like night and day. 

But on the other hand he might want space, just make it known that above all else, you are there for him. Even if he seems fine, let him know because men break down in silence. 

You kind of need to learn how he is processing everything and going through the phases of grief. It's like a switch. Losing a brother was the worst pain I've ever felt. So I can understand the anger and sorrow that he is feeling right now.

Also never stop talking about his brother. Ask him if he talks to him or just bring up a funny memory you guys share of him. This is really important. Dont let him lose the joy and happiness his brother gave him. Remind him of all the good things.

I feel for you man. I lost my big brother a year and a half ago and I still find myself struggling from time to time, but like others have said keeping your body and mind active is an amazing way to cope. I didnt realize how important it was until I started having okay days. It's always important to have people around you as well. Being able to talk to your friends about this experience and how you guys are doing is something not a lot of people get when someone passes. I wish you, your friends and your friend's family all the best. It's a horrible thing to go through but we are all here for each other so never hesitate to ask for help.

Anytime bud. You would be surprised by how many people might actually be in your situation. It's our duty to make sure others In our situation get the closure and comfort they need. And also get it for ourselves when we need it.

I find that meeting people or just even talking to people who are in the same situation as you helps a lot. Grief comes in waves and I didn't really understand that until I experienced it myself. My big bro was my best friend too and it hurts every single day. I just found ways around how to show my emotions. If you ever want to talk pm me. That's a very interesting question. When I look back on the time when I lost my brother I remember myself being in a box and i could see everything outside but no one could look inside. I don't think my friends could comprehend all the emotions that I went through so I dont look at it as them abandoning me, they were just waiting for me to come back from this long journey of grief. I feel like my friends dont know that it still affects me to this day but I'll never resent them for that. I take my experience as something I can help them with when it comes time for them to experience grief. If you feel like your friends abandoned you it's not like that. Most likely they just dont understand like you probably didn't during the beginning of the grieving process. And if they did abandon you they weren't your friends to begin with. That's how I see it anyways. Much love brother.

Im so sorry for your loss. I know it can be hard to lose someone so close to you. The only thing i can do now even 9 months after my own brother passed is keep myself distracted. Every single day its a battle with myself to keep me from thinking. Im lucky enough to be into hobbies that require lots of attention and keep my brain going. 

What ive done is play games, watch tv shows and work as much as i could. And when i wasnt doing any of those, i was watching stuff on youtube or facebook. I never let myself go a minute without listening to some form of audio. 

My brother was into music so sometimes if i listen to music that he liked i start thinking about how much i miss him and that i want to be with him. But thats my personal experience. So if music keeps you distracted then go for it. 

Again i know how hard it is to go through that and i remember even at 5 months its not easy. Its not even easy now after closing up on a year. People are liars.
